title: The Friday surah
hook: many read al-Kahf every Friday, a practice drawn from hadith (Hakim; Bayhaqi)
tomorrow: The young men in the cave

segments.voice: Yesterday, Fajr, the dawn recitation, and your line was dawn is witnessed. Did you say your line this morning before the phone? What was the quiet like? Day four hundred sixty-three, and a new surah.

A Friday morning, a mosque, an hour before the noon prayer. Along the walls, people sit alone, each with a Qur'an open to the same place. Ask one of them and you may hear: it's Friday, so it's al-Kahf. Surah eighteen. The Cave. A surah with a weekly appointment. Some read it in Arabic, some in translation, some under their breath. Today, before we open its stories, where that appointment comes from.

The custom rests on a hadith recorded by al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi: whoever reads Surat al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for them between the two Fridays. A week of light, from one reading to the next. Hadith scholars have discussed how strong its chains are, and the practice has lasted. Because the Islamic day begins at sunset, some read it on Thursday night, others on Friday itself. Another hadith, in Sahih Muslim, says that whoever memorizes the first ten verses of al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal, the great deceiver of the end of time. That's one reason some families teach those ten verses early. And Bukhari tells a scene: a companion was reciting al-Kahf at night, his horse tied nearby, and a cloud came down over him and began to circle; the horse grew restless. In the morning he told the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, who said: that was the sakinah, the tranquility, which came down for the Qur'an. The surah opens, in Pickthall's words: "Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed therein any crookedness". Then come four long stories: young men who hide in a cave, a man with two gardens, Musa traveling to learn from a stranger, and a powerful traveler who builds a wall. Some teachers today read them as four trials: of faith, of wealth, of knowledge, and of power. That framing is a modern reading, not a hadith, but it helps hold the surah in your head. For the next week, we'll walk through it, one story at a time.

segments.voice: The practice is to plan to read it this Friday. Sit, and think through your coming Friday. Where's a half hour that could belong to al-Kahf? Before work, at lunch, after the noon prayer, on the train. If the whole surah feels like a lot, plan for the first ten, in Arabic or in translation. Picture where you'll sit and what the page will look like. If you pray, you can ask for that week of light. The bell holds the time.
Al-Kahf. The Cave, read each week by many Muslims for a light that lasts from one Friday to the next. Today's word.
Your line: friday's surah. Today, put it in your calendar: a time, a place, and the first ten verses at least. Day four hundred sixty-three.

howItsDone: Many Muslims read Surat al-Kahf every Friday, or from Thursday sunset, alone or in groups at the mosque; some also memorize its first ten verses, following the hadith in Sahih Muslim.
